title: Keep Agent Memory Across Sessions
oneLiner: Store what the agent learned outside the context window so the next run does not start from zero.
audience: Builders running multi-day research, support, or account workflows.
intro: Context windows are working memory, not storage. A session that ends takes everything the agent inferred with it unless you write it somewhere durable.
requirements: A persistence layer: SQLite, Postgres, or the memory blocks your framework provides
A defined rule for what gets written and what gets discarded
A way to inspect and correct stored memory

sections.heading: Decide what is worth persisting
sections.body: Store facts that will still be true next week: account identifiers, approved preferences, and completed steps. Do not persist raw conversation, which grows without adding durable value.

sections.heading: Make memory readable by a human
sections.body: Letta splits memory into labeled blocks the agent can edit. Readable blocks let you catch a corrupted fact before it shapes ten more answers; opaque embeddings do not.

sections.heading: Version the write path
sections.body: A memory update is a write to state you will later trust. Log the change, keep the previous value, and make the correction path as easy as the create path.

sections.heading: Test recall with a fixed question set
sections.body: Ask the same five questions at the start of a session and compare answers over time. That is a cheaper signal than reading transcripts, and it catches silent memory drift.

checklist: Durable facts are written outside the context window.
Each memory block or record has an owner and an update time.
A human can review and correct stored memory.
A fixed recall question set is checked after changes.
